event_ts.description: Vendor timestamp, ISO-8601 UTC. Null when the record carried none.

event_type.description: Which of the event types below this is; selects how `payload` reads.

parent_id.description: The id of the record this one answered or followed (`parentUuid`), forming the session DAG. Null at a session root.

record_id.description: This event's own id, from the vendor record (`uuid`). Null for derived events that had no record of their own.

api_error.description: A provider-side failure returned instead of a response.

error_class.description: Bucketed failure kind derived from the HTTP status: `rate_limit` (429), `overloaded` (529), and so on.

provider_request_id.description: The provider's request id, for correlating with their logs.

raw.description: The complete original vendor record, after scrubbing. The losslessness backstop: anything not promoted to a field is still here.

retry_after_ms.description: Backoff the provider asked for, in milliseconds.

retry_count.description: How many attempts had already been made when this error was recorded.

retryable.description: Whether the provider marked the failure as worth retrying.

assistant_message.description: One assistant record. A single API response is split across several of these; see `message_id`.

attribution_agent.description: The agent type whose instructions produced this record — `general-purpose`, or a named subagent. Only ever set on a subagent sidechain, so null means the main session.

attribution_plugin.description: The plugin supplying the skill in force, when one was.

attribution_skill.description: The skill whose instructions were in force for this record, `plugin:skill` when it came from a plugin. This is what answers "which skills did this work actually use" — distinct from the `skill_listing` attachment, which only says which skills were offered in context.

block_types.description: Ordered list of this record's content block types, exactly as emitted. Finer-grained than `content_kind` -- use it to tell `redacted_thinking` from `thinking`.

cache_miss_tokens.description: Always null: Claude Code's usage object does not expose it.

cache_read_tokens.description: Tokens served from cache. Response-scoped -- see `usage_scope`.

cache_write_detail.description: Per-TTL breakdown of what was written to cache. Absent when the vendor reported no breakdown.

cache_write_detail[].tokens.description: Tokens written to cache at this TTL.

cache_write_tokens.description: Total tokens written to cache, all TTLs. Response-scoped -- see `usage_scope`.

content_kind.description: Coarse shape of this record: `text`, `thinking`, `tool_use`, `mixed`, or `empty`. Lets a consumer tell a reasoning step from a final answer without parsing `raw`.

duration_ms.description: Always null on an assistant record: Claude Code times tool calls, not turns.

effort.description: The reasoning-effort setting for this response, when the vendor recorded one.

estimated_visible_tokens.description: Tokenizer count of this record's visible output -- reply text plus tool names and arguments. Thinking blocks are excluded, and a thinking-only record therefore reads 0. **An estimate, not Claude's own count**: produced by `output_tokenizer` (OpenAI's vocabulary), which runs about 1.13x under Claude on Sonnet 4.6 and 1.52x under on the Claude 5 family. Stored raw with no multiplier applied so the ratio can be re-applied later. Counted before redaction, so a scrubbed Write body still counts. See docs/design/notes/claude_token_usage.md.

first_block_of_message.description: True on exactly one event per API response. The dedup selector: sum a token field only where this is true and you get the response total, since usage is repeated on every record of the response.

has_thinking.description: Whether the model reasoned in this record. With the plaintext stripped by the vendor and the signature dropped on the way into `raw`, this flag plus the record's position is the remaining signal.

message_id.description: Groups the several records the vendor split one API response into. The key for any response-level aggregation.

output_tokenizer.description: Which tokenizer produced `estimated_visible_tokens`, e.g. `o200k_base`. Ships per event because a token count means nothing without the vocabulary behind it, and that vocabulary will eventually change.

output_tokens.description: Tokens produced -- **including thinking**, which is billed here and never broken out. Response-scoped; see `usage_scope`. Subtract the visible estimate to recover the thinking share.

provider_request_id.description: The vendor's own per-call request id (`req_...`, distinct from `message_id`'s `msg_...`), present on essentially every response. The join key to OTel's own `request_id` attribute (`config/otel/claude_code.yaml`) -- what lets a JSONL-only session be priced from tokens alone via the request-level join (`worker/otel_trueup.py`), independent of whether OTel telemetry is also running.

raw.description: The complete original vendor record, after scrubbing. The losslessness backstop: anything not promoted to a field is still here.

reasoning_tokens.description: Always null here. Not unknowable -- it is recovered by summing `estimated_visible_tokens` across a `message_id` and subtracting from `output_tokens` -- but that spans records, so the graph layer derives it rather than this event holding a partial answer.

stop_reason.description: Why generation stopped: `tool_use`, `end_turn`, `stop_sequence`. **Null means this record is not the final one** of its response and its usage numbers are not yet settled.

text_char_count.description: Length of the concatenated text blocks, measured on the unscrubbed record so volume survives the cap. Null when there is no text block; 0 means a text block that is empty.

text_truncated.description: Whether `assistant_text_len` clipped the text stored in `raw`. `text_char_count` still reports the full original length.

thinking_char_count.description: Length of the thinking plaintext. Null means no thinking block; 0 means one is present but empty, which is what every observed Claude Code version writes. The distinction is the point.

tool_arg_chars.description: Serialized length of this record's tool names and arguments, unscrubbed. The character-level companion to `estimated_visible_tokens`.

tool_call_count.description: Tool-use blocks in **this record**, not the whole response. Needed because each call costs a fixed block of output tokens beyond its arguments.

usage_scope.description: Always `response`: the token fields on this event describe the whole API response, not this record's blocks. They are correct, just scoped wider than the event carrying them.

attachment.description: Context injected outside the message flow: @-mentioned files, IDE state, skill listings, hook output.

added_names.description: Tool names newly made available to the model.

artifact_class.description: What kind of thing this is -- `code`, `documentation`, `config` -- from the path or MIME type. Null when unclassified.

attachment_type.description: The vendor's own label for this injection, e.g. `skill_listing`, `file`, `hook_success`.

content_chars.description: Length of the injected body before any cap, so a clipped body is never mistaken for a short one.

content_truncated.description: Whether the body in `raw` was clipped by the attachment cap.

display_path.description: Path as shown to the model, which may be relative or abbreviated.

extension.description: File extension, kept raw alongside `artifact_class` so a taxonomy change can be re-applied without re-ingesting.

hook_event.description: Which lifecycle point fired the hook, e.g. `SessionStart`.

hook_name.description: Name of the hook that produced this.

is_startup_context.description: Whether this arrived as part of session startup rather than mid-conversation. CLAUDE.md arrives this way, via the SessionStart hook.

item_count.description: Number of items in a reminder listing.

line_end.description: Last line of the selected range.

line_start.description: First line of the selected range.

new_date.description: The date the session rolled over to.

path.description: Filesystem path of the attached file.

raw.description: The complete original vendor record, after scrubbing. The losslessness backstop: anything not promoted to a field is still here.

removed_names.description: Tool names withdrawn from the model.

skill_names.description: Which skills were in context. Kept even when the listing body is dropped, because this is the part worth querying.

total_lines.description: Line count of the attached file.

compaction.description: The session transcript was summarized to reclaim context.

raw.description: The complete original vendor record, after scrubbing. The losslessness backstop: anything not promoted to a field is still here.

trigger.description: What caused it: automatic threshold or an explicit request.

file_change.description: A file the session created, edited or deleted. Derived from a tool call, not a vendor record.

artifact_class.description: What kind of file this is -- `code`, `documentation`, `config` -- from its path.

derived_from_event_id.description: The `tool_call` event this was derived from. This event has no vendor record of its own.

hunks.description: Edited regions. The only per-call signal of edit size -- the vendor sets no line-count field on an Edit/Write result (0 of 1,690 checked).

hunks[].len.description: Lines the region occupies AFTER the edit.

hunks[].old_len.description: Lines it occupied before. `len - old_len` is the net change; without it a hunk says where an edit landed but not how much it moved.

hunks[].start.description: First line of the region, after the edit.

lines_added.description: Exact count of added (`+`) lines, from the structuredPatch diff body before it is dropped. The gross code-churn signal the hunk sizes cannot give (they include unchanged context).

lines_removed.description: Exact count of removed (`-`) lines, from the structuredPatch diff body.

message_id.description: The API response whose tool call produced this change.

operation.description: What happened to the file: create, edit or delete.

path.description: Filesystem path of the changed file.

raw.description: The complete original vendor record, after scrubbing. The losslessness backstop: anything not promoted to a field is still here.

pr_link.description: Claude Code's own note of a pull request it opened, carrying the fully-qualified repository and PR number/url.

pr_repository.description: The fully-qualified `owner/name` the PR was opened against -- the highest-provenance repository identity in the transcript.

raw.description: The complete original vendor record, after scrubbing. The losslessness backstop: anything not promoted to a field is still here.

session_start.description: Opens a session. One per transcript, carrying session-wide identity.

ai_title.description: The vendor's own one-line summary of what the session is about. Repeated on many records; captured once here.

attribution_agent.description: The agent type this stream is running as, for a subagent session. Null on a master session — every record carrying it is on a sidechain, so the null is the discriminator rather than a gap.

cwd.description: Working directory the session ran in.

git_branch.description: Branch checked out at session start.

git_remote.description: The `cwd`'s real git remote, from the upload manifest's per-file `repo_url` (preferred) or `repo` -- captured by the uploader client via a real `git remote get-url origin` run at the session's actual working directory, and matched onto this session by the manifest entry the collector read it from (not a separate cwd-keyed lookup). Null when the manifest carried no repo for this file, `cwd` wasn't a git repo, or it had no `origin`. The evidence-ladder's `remote` tier prefers this over anything scraped from a transcript's own tool calls (`worker/graph_fold.py::repo_info`).

parent_session_id.description: The session that spawned this one, for subagent transcripts. Null for a top-level session.

raw.description: The complete original vendor record, after scrubbing. The losslessness backstop: anything not promoted to a field is still here.

repo_id.description: Always null: no stable repository identity is derivable yet.

sub_agent_spawn.description: An Agent/Task tool call that started a child session with its own transcript.

agent_type.description: Which agent was asked for, e.g. `Explore`, `general-purpose`.

child_session_id.description: The child's own transcript id, linking to its events.

description.description: Short label for the delegated task.

duration_ms.description: How long the child ran. Null while still running or if never paired.

message_id.description: The API response that requested the spawn.

prompt_char_count.description: Length of the instruction given to the child, measured unscrubbed.

raw.description: The complete original vendor record, after scrubbing. The losslessness backstop: anything not promoted to a field is still here.

requested_model.description: Model asked for. May differ from what actually ran.

resolved_model.description: Model the child actually used. Children routinely differ from the parent, which is why their cost cannot be assumed.

run_in_background.description: Whether the parent continued without waiting.

status.description: Outcome once the child finished. Null while pending.

tool_call.description: A tool invocation the model requested, enriched in place with its result.

bytes_read.description: UTF-8 size of the tool's **result**, not of any file on disk. Present once the result is paired.

duration_ms.description: How long the tool took. Frequently null even on a matched result -- only present when the vendor reported it.

exit_status.description: Process exit status for tools that run commands.

files.description: Files this call touched, one entry each.

files[].description: One file touched by the call.

files[].artifact_class.description: What kind of file, from its path or MIME type.

files[].bytes.description: Size of the file content involved.

files[].extension.description: File extension, kept raw alongside the class.

files[].hunks.description: Edited regions within this file. See `file_change.hunks`.

files[].hunks[].len.description: Lines the region occupies AFTER the edit.

files[].hunks[].old_len.description: Lines it occupied before; `len - old_len` is the net change.

files[].hunks[].start.description: First line of the region, after the edit.

files[].lines_added.description: Exact count of added (`+`) lines, from the structuredPatch diff body. The gross code-churn signal the hunk sizes cannot give (they include context).

files[].lines_removed.description: Exact count of removed (`-`) lines, from the structuredPatch diff body.

files[].mime_type.description: MIME type, the only signal for remote artifacts that never produce a local file.

files[].operation.description: What happened to this file: read, create, edit or delete.

files[].path.description: Local path. Null for remote artifacts reached through MCP.

files[].remote_id.description: Identifier for a remote artifact, e.g. a Google Doc id.

input.description: The tool's arguments, verbatim and vendor-shaped. Deliberately opaque: descending into it would pin a vendor's structure as if it were ours. Generated file content is scrubbed when configured.

input_chars.description: Serialized length of `input` before any scrub, so redacted arguments still report their true size.

mcp_server.description: For an MCP tool, which server provided it.

mcp_tool.description: For an MCP tool, the tool name within that server.

message_id.description: The API response that requested this call.

raw.description: The complete original vendor record, after scrubbing. The losslessness backstop: anything not promoted to a field is still here.

tool_name.description: Tool invoked, as the model named it.

tool_result.description: The result record paired to a tool call; carries the outcome, never the content.

raw.description: The complete original vendor record, after scrubbing. The losslessness backstop: anything not promoted to a field is still here.

source_tool_assistant_uuid.description: The assistant record that issued the call, when the vendor recorded it.

tool_denial_kind.description: Why a call was refused, when it was: the user declined, a permission rule blocked it, and so on. Null when the call was not denied.

unknown.description: A record type the normalizer does not map. Kept whole in `raw` so nothing is lost.

raw.description: The complete original vendor record, after scrubbing. The losslessness backstop: anything not promoted to a field is still here.

user_message.description: A turn from the user side -- either typed by a person or injected by the harness.

char_count.description: Length of the message before any cap, measured unscrubbed.

is_injected.description: **True means the harness produced this, not a person** -- a skill body, a system reminder, command output, a task notification. Typed prompts are the primary intent signal; injected ones are context. Filter on this before treating a user message as intent.

permission_mode.description: The permission mode in force when this prompt was sent: `auto`, `plan`, `acceptEdits` or `default`. Stamped on the record by the vendor, so no correlation with neighbouring mode records is needed. Single-valued across every turn measured, so it describes the turn rather than the individual record. Null on records from before the vendor emitted it.

plan_mode.description: True when the prompt was sent in plan mode — `permission_mode == 'plan'`, kept as its own boolean because "was this planning or doing" is the common filter. Null, not False, when the vendor recorded no mode at all: unknown and not-plan-mode are different claims.

raw.description: The complete original vendor record, after scrubbing. The losslessness backstop: anything not promoted to a field is still here.

text.description: Message text, capped for injected messages and kept whole for typed ones.

text_truncated.description: Whether `text` was clipped. `char_count` still reports the full length.
